CFML Language Reference: Functions

FormatBaseN

Converts a number to its representation in base 2 through 36. Digits beyond 9 are written as lowercase letters (a = 10, b = 11, ... z = 35).

Category

Mathematical functions

Syntax

FormatBaseN(number, radix)

Parameters

number
The number to convert. Any fractional part is discarded.
radix
The base, from 2 to 36.

Returns

A string. Negative numbers get a leading minus sign.

Usage

A radix outside 2-36 raises an Expression error. Use InputBaseN to convert back to decimal. Base 16 is useful for HTML colors: Right("0" & FormatBaseN(n, 16), 2) gives two hex digits.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>number</TH><TH>Base 2</TH><TH>Base 8</TH><TH>Base 16</TH><TH>Base 36</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="n" LIST="10,255,1999,-42">
<CFOUTPUT><TR><TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#n#</TD><TD><TT>#FormatBaseN(n, 2)#</TT></TD><TD><TT>#FormatBaseN(n, 8)#</TT></TD>
<TD><TT>#FormatBaseN(n, 16)#</TT></TD><TD><TT>#FormatBaseN(n, 36)#</TT></TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<P>A web-safe palette row:
<CFLOOP INDEX="g" FROM="0" TO="255" STEP="51">
<CFSET hex = Right("0" & FormatBaseN(g, 16), 2)>
<CFOUTPUT><FONT COLOR="##00#hex#00"><B>##00#hex#00</B></FONT> </CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
